To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is possible (1) to decode spoken and imagined words from brain activity, (2) to discriminate the vowel and consonants in words from brain activity and (3) to define the cortical areas that carry the most information about the vowels and consonant of imagined and spoken words.

it is possible, using signals recorded from the brain's surface, to decode the vowels and consonant of both spoken and imagined words, and that the decoding performance is highest in the superior temporal gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus.
we can decode spoken and imagined words from the surface of a person’s brain, and we can identify which cortical regions contain the most information for decoding vowels and consonants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of human brain function.
how the brain encodes speech sounds and how this information can be decoded.
the neural mechanisms of speech and reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it is possible for the first time to decode the vowels and consonant sounds in imagined and spoken words using brain signals.
it is possible, in principle, to decode the speech of others, and possibly even one's own thoughts, using brain signals.
we have shown that it is possible for humans to decode the vowels and consonant sounds of spoken and imagined words, using signals recorded from the brain's surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible for humans to decode the speech of other humans by reading brain activity.
it is possible, using brain signals, to decode imagined speech.
it is possible, at least in principle, to decode imagined speech from brain signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a 'black box'.
the brain is a very complex system that is not yet well understood and that it will take many years of research before we are able to decode the meaning of words from brain signals.
it is indeed possible to decode speech from brain signals.
